subject: microglobal function for several points of presence

messages.author: e2b7ce96be7db2cd
messages.subject: microglobal function for several points of presence
parts:
Hi! I`m just learning about NicheMapR.
I have computed the function "microglobal" for one point or presence. But, when I use several points, R says:

"extracting climate data
no climate data for this site, using dummy data so solar is still produced extracting soil moisture data Sorry, there is no environmental data for this location running microclimate model for 12 days by 5 years at site long -67.295166 lat -67.52816 Note: the output column `SOLR` in metout and shadmet is for unshaded horizontal plane solar radiation runtime 1.46999999997206 seconds"

Also, whatever the way I compute microglobal (one or several points of presence), I obtain layers. Then, I rewrite the "metout/soilmoist/etc" layers into a .asc format; but it seems the results are not the best. Layers .asc have strange values; if I try to print them in QGIS, they do not. 

I have many more doubts, but I will start with these ones. 

I really appreciate If you can help me.

Luciana.

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: microglobal function for several points of presence
parts:
Hi Luciana,

You can only run the microclimate model at one site at a time. If you want to do multiple sites, you need to set it to run in a loop through each site. I'll post some code shortly to the group to show how to do this over a grid of points. Note that the output of the micro_ functions is a list, not a layer. E.g., one item in the list is 'soil' which is a table of soil temperature with time at different depths. Have a close look at this vignette if you haven't already and see if it helps. If you are still having trouble, post a reproducible example of the code you're trying to make it easier to advise on what might be going wrong.

All the best,
Mike

messages.author: e2b7ce96be7db2cd
messages.subject: Re: microglobal function for several points of presence
parts:
Hi Mike!
Thanks for your response. I will run the microclimate model at one site at a time. 
Now, the other (and very important) question is what can I do to display climate suitability maps (species model distribution) using the microclimate and ectotherm information? I mean, How can I use or transform these lists (soilshade, metout, etc) into something accurate to use with points of presence and obtain these maps? (I am working with anuran tadpoles)
 
My code looks like that: 
install.packages("NicheMapR")
install.packages('devtools')
get.global.climate(folder="c:/global_climate")

library(NicheMapR)
longlat <- c(-67.295166, -31.021580) #Ir sitio por sitio
micro <- micro_global(loc=longlat, timeinterval=12, nyears=5, rainmult=2,8, snowmodel=0, rainfrac=0.1, minshade=0, maxshade=90)
View(micro)

# retrieve output
metout <- as.data.frame(micro$metout) # above ground microclimatic conditions, min shade
shadmet <- as.data.frame(micro$shadmet) # above ground microclimatic conditions, max shade
soil <- as.data.frame(micro$soil) # soil temperatures, minimum shade
shadsoil <- as.data.frame(micro$shadsoil)# soil temperatures, maximum shade
soilmoist <- as.data.frame(micro$soilmoist)

# append dates
dates <- micro$dates
metout <- cbind(dates, metout)
soil <- cbind(dates, soil)
shadmet <- cbind(dates, shadmet)
shadsoil <- cbind(dates, shadsoil)

# modelo ectotermo- Poner las variables segun la población(sitio)
ecto <- ectotherm (Ww_g=0.037, shape=2, CT_max=43.56, CT_min=3.88, diurn=1, nocturn=1)
View(ecto)

# retrieve output
environ <- as.data.frame(ecto$environ)# activity, Tb and environment
View(environ)
soilmoist <- as.data.frame(ecto$soilmoist)
View(soilmoist)

#Convertir un archivo del dataframe en .asc
capa1 <- metout
nrows <- nrow(capa1)
ncols <- ncol(capa1)
r <- raster(nrows = nrows, ncols = ncols)
extent(r) <- c(-67.295166, ncols, -31.021580, nrows)
values(r) <- as.vector(t(capa1))
res(r) <- c(1, 1)
writeRaster(r, filename = "capa1Ra.asc", format = "ascii", overwrite = TRUE)

capa2 <- environ
nrows <- nrow(capa2)
ncols <- ncol(capa2)
r <- raster(nrows = nrows, ncols = ncols)
extent(r) <- c(-67.295166, ncols, -31.021580, nrows)
values(r) <- as.vector(t(capa2))
res(r) <- c(1, 1)
writeRaster(r, filename = "capa2Ra.asc", format = "ascii", overwrite = TRUE)

capa3 <- soilmoist
nrows <- nrow(capa3)
ncols <- ncol(capa3)
r <- raster(nrows = nrows, ncols = ncols)
extent(r) <- c(-67.295166, ncols, -31.021580, nrows)
values(r) <- as.vector(t(capa3))
res(r) <- c(1, 1)
writeRaster(r, filename = "capa3Ra.asc", format = "ascii", overwrite = TRUE)

The #Convertir un archivo del dataframe en .asc is the way I find to transform the lists into .asc files. I thought it was ok.

Anyway, any help would be welcome. 
Thanks.

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: microglobal function for several points of presence
parts:
Hi Luciana,
I just posted a general example of running the microclimate model (and ectotherm model) over a grid of points. Hopefully that answers your question.
All the best,
Mike

p.s. I saw that you were specifying the CT_min and CT_max values in your run of the ectotherm model - they only really affect how deep the animal goes below ground to avoid extremes. If you haven't had much experience with this kind of model it is worth spending a good chunk of time learning the ins and outs of how it works, and the effects of the different parameters, as there is a lot going on and it's easy to end up with biologically unrealistic simulations
